title: test(console): pin that a FormPage row with a retired field type renders the tombstone, not a control
body:
Fixes #10176
Clause-②: no

## Summary

The card's defect is already gone on `main`. objectui#10457 (squash commit `212c45175`) repaired it when it replaced `FormPage`'s own `switch (field.type)` with the shared resolver. That resolver answers a retired spelling with the tombstone. This PR is the pin alone: one new test suite and an empty-frontmatter changeset. No source file changes.

## Step 1: measured on current `main`, before any edit

Measured by rendering `FormPage` with real widgets, the way `FormPage.sharedWidgets-10179.test.tsx` does, over an object with two fields: `who` of `type: 'owner'` and `title` of `type: 'text'`. Both routes were driven: `/forms/:name` (internal) and `/f/:slug` (public). Measured with a throwaway probe file. It was deleted afterwards and is not in this PR.

GitHub strips tag-shaped text from PR bodies, so each element is written as `TAG[attributes]` below, and nesting is written in words. Class lists are left out. Everything else is the render output exactly.

**On `main` at `808f33986`**, which contains `212c45175`. `FormPage.tsx` there is byte-identical to `212c45175` (`git diff --stat 212c45175 808f33986 -- apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` is empty). The output was the same on both routes:

```text
owner row: DIV holding two children
  LABEL[for="f_who"] "Who"
  DIV[role="alert", data-testid="field-retired-tombstone", data-retired-field-type="owner"]
    "[object-ui] Field type `owner` was RETIRED (objectui#4814). It was a synonym for `user` with no behavioral difference, and it is not a member of `@objectstack/spec`'s FieldType. Write the record-owner field as `{ type: 'user', name: 'owner' }` — the field NAME carries the ownership meaning, the type carries the widget. The `widget: 'field:owner'` spelling is retired with it."
text row: DIV holding two children
  LABEL[for="f_title"] "Title"
  INPUT[id="f_title", aria-invalid="false", type="text", value="", name="title"]
form input, select and textarea count: 1   (the Title row)
input[type=text] count:                1
tombstones:                            1
```

**Pre-fix control leg, on `061f5e829`**, the only parent of `212c45175`. Same probe, in a detached comparison worktree that was removed afterwards. The output was the same on both routes:

```text
owner row: DIV holding two children
  LABEL[for="f_who"] "Who"
  INPUT[id="f_who", type="text", value="", name="who"]
text row: DIV holding two children
  LABEL[for="f_title"] "Title"
  INPUT[id="f_title", type="text", value="", name="title"]
form input, select and textarea count: 2
input[type=text] count:                2
tombstones:                            0
```

So the card's measurement was right for the tree it was taken on. The commit that made `owner` refuse visibly on this page is `212c45175` (objectui#10457). `FormPage.tsx` has not changed since that commit.

## The pin: `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.retiredFieldType-10176.test.tsx`

- **Where the retired set comes from.** `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES` is read at runtime from `@object-ui/fields`. That is the table the resolver consults: it lives in `@object-ui/core`, and `@object-ui/fields` re-exports it. It is not copied into the test. It does not come from `@objectstack/spec`: the installed spec (`17.4.0`) has no retired-field-type table. A search of its `dist` finds no such symbol, while `FieldType` is found in the same files. `owner` was never a spec `FieldType` member. Measured at `0154a6588`, the table has no member other than `owner`, so no second retired type exists to drive. The suite drives every key of the table, so a type retired later is covered with no edit to the test. A population check asserts that the table is non-empty and contains `owner`.
- **Retired leg (per key, per route).** The retired row must render the tombstone with `role="alert"` and `data-retired-field-type` set to the spelling. It must also contain no editable control, which the `EDITABLE_CONTROL` query checks: inputs, selects, textareas, buttons, `contenteditable`, and the textbox, combobox, listbox, spinbutton, slider, switch, checkbox and radio roles. All three facts are asserted as one object, so a failure reports all of them together.
- **Control leg (per route).** A live `text` row in the same form must render an enabled textbox named by its label, and the same `EDITABLE_CONTROL` query must match it. That shows the "no editable control" check can fire.
- The prescription text is not pinned. The test asserts the kind of element (`role="alert"`) and the spelling it names (`data-retired-field-type`).

## Ablation (committed state `0154a6588`, restored by blob)

The mutation was made with `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, under a restore trap. It changed `FormPage.tsx`'s `resolveFieldWidgetKey` so that it points `owner` at the `text` widget:

- anchor `return resolveFormWidgetType(field.type);`, replaced by `return field.type === 'owner' ? 'text' : resolveFormWidgetType(field.type);`
- on-disk proof: anchor count 1 to 0, injected count 0 to 1, blob `42878cef4992` to `1bc40cbb1572`. Both counts and the blob were read again from disk inside the wrapped command before vitest ran.
- result: **2 failed, 3 passed**. Both retired legs went red (`/forms/:name` and `/f/:slug`) with:
  ```text
  - "editableControls": 0,   "tombstoneNames": "owner", "tombstoneRole": "alert"
  + "editableControls": 1,   "tombstoneNames": null,    "tombstoneRole": null
  ```
  Both control legs and the population check stayed green.
- restore: the blob is `42878cef4992` again, equal to the `HEAD` blob. `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty.

## Gates (all at `0154a6588`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/components/` from the repo root: **30 of 30 files and 403 of 403 tests passed**. There are 30 test files on disk under that directory, 21 of them `FormPage.*`, so every `FormPage` suite ran.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` (the console's own script, `tsc --noEmit && tsc -b tsconfig.node.json --force`): exit 0. It ran after `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...'`, which built 34 of 34 tasks. `tsc --noEmit --listFiles` confirms that the program includes the new test file and resolves `@object-ui/fields` to the built `packages/fields/dist/index.d.ts`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. It reports that 1 released package's source changed and that the 1 changeset declared has an empty frontmatter.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: exit 0. It prints "No pending changeset names a file this change touches."
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations, exit 0.
- Also run, because the diff touches a test with a `vi.mock` and a changeset: `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `check-changeset-no-major`. All exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on both paths reports NOT GOVERNED.
- ESLint on the touched test file, from `apps/console`, which picks up the root `eslint.config.js`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, and no messages under any rule. At base the file did not exist, so every per-rule delta is 0. The effective config has 96 active rules, including `object-ui/no-line-address-in-test-name`. Its `parserOptions` are empty, so type-aware linting is off, and a new file cannot move the verdict on any other file. `FormPage.sharedWidgets-10179.test.tsx` was linted in the same run as a control and also has 0 messages.

## Acceptance notes

- **Changeset.** The dispatch expected that a test-only change needs no changeset. The presence gate disagrees: it reads any file under `apps/console/src/` as released source, test files included, and its header says there is "No carve-out for test files under `src/`". So this PR adds `.changeset/10176-formpage-retired-type-pin.md` with an empty frontmatter, which declares that nothing is released. The claim's file surface names that changeset.
- **Observation, not filed.** On the retired row, `LABEL[for="f_who"]` names no element, because the tombstone takes no `id` (see the step 1 output). The refusal is still announced through `role="alert"`. The pin does not assert either way on the id, so it does not lock this in.
- Two related widget-axis readings from the same probe are handed to the seat in the report. They are not addressed here: the tombstone's naming when the retired spelling comes through `widget`, and the text fallback for an unregistered `widget`.

Implemented by the `domain:ui` seat 1 dispatch, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`.
